newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson seeking fewer air cargo carriers.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson seeking fewer air cargo carriers.

text.p: The public telecoms unit of Sweden telecommunications company L.M. Ericsson said on Tuesday it is seeking to reduce the number of prime carriers it uses for air cargo to two or three.

Lars-Olof Bjorklund, Manager of Export Operations at Ericsson Telecom, told an air cargo seminar in Gothenburg that Ericsson currently mainly used four carriers, including KLM, Lufthansa and Air France.
"We want to focus on a couple of prime carriers for global coverage," he told the seminar.
Bjorklund told Reuters that Ericsson, which is one of Sweden's biggest exporters, had strategic carriers it used as well as prime carriers which could offer complete global coverage.
Strategic carriers could offer strong coverage of a specific region.
The Ericsson official was criticial of airlines that he said did not want to discuss long-term strategic cooperation.
"We have wanted to talk about long term agreements but suppliers only wanted to talk in times of economic downturn. When the good times come back then they do not want to know," he said.
He said building long term relations with carriers was the only way forward.
"It is time for the carriers and forwarders to recognise that this is the only way to behave to achieve quality and cost effectiveness," he added.
He said Ericsson had set itself strategic goals of cutting delivery lead times to 24 hours for Nordic customers, 48 hours for European customers and 72 hours for inter-continental deliveries.
This had already been achieved in some areas but there was no specific timeframe. "We have been saying 2000 plus until now but we are already there with some areas."
